style: Neutral Latin American Spanish for a friendly chess coaching app. Address the reader as tú. Short, warm, natural spoken sentences, the way a good coach talks. Never use em dashes; use commas, colons or full stops. No filler phrases. Latin American rules (from doblarr's subtitle corpus): use ustedes, never vosotros or its verb forms; prefer the simple past (¿qué pasó?, not ¿qué ha pasado?); say ir por, never ir a por; never use vale for okay (use bien, está bien, listo); NEVER use coger for take or capture (use tomar, capturar, comer); avoid Spain-only words such as coche, móvil, ordenador, guay, pillar, apetece, tío, joder; prefer neutral words understood everywhere (auto, computadora, celular).

terms.queen: dama (reina is fine in casual coach speech)
terms.kingside / queenside: flanco de rey / flanco de dama

keep: Keep exactly as written: square names (e4, f7), move notation (Nf3, Qxd8+, O-O, 1.e4, 14...c4), the token [move], {{placeholders}}, <tags> and </tags>, numbers, people's names, and names of openings and games that are usually kept in English (but translate descriptive opening names that have a standard Spanish name, e.g. Italian Game = Apertura Italiana, Queen's Gambit = Gambito de Dama, Sicilian Defense = Defensa Siciliana, French Defense = Defensa Francesa, Ruy Lopez = Apertura Española).
